page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top centre. Page number top right. Main text in roman and italic, one column of paragraphs. A large woodcut initial "O" at the start of the concio. Heading "CONCIO XXXVIII" with the scripture reference "Eccles. 26." below it, both centred. No marginal notes and no notes under the text.

main_text.p: ornamentum est: at pudenda, est quasi quod dampnus in eius membris. Et Prouerb. 21. & 25. Praestat in angulo tecti degere, quàm vxorem habere rixosam, & domum communem. vel, quam cum muliere rixosa in domo ampla. i. Melius est habitare incommodissimè sine rixis, quàm commodissimè cum rixosa coniuge. Et cap. 30. Si morosa nupserit, perturbat terram. Deus & pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi, à quo descendit omnis datio bona, & omne donum perfectum, det omni petenti bonam & fortem vxorem, & omni habenti vxorem malam & dissolutam, Iobi sapientiam & patientiam. Amen.
main_text.head: CONCIO XXXVIII

p.i: OMITAS vxoris delectat virum suum, & ossa ipsius pinguefacit eiusdem peritia. vxor taciturna & cordata donum Dei est, nec est quo pretio permutes eruditam animam. Gratia alia super aliam est vxor pudens & fidelis, nec tanti ponatur est vllum, vt eo rependas animi ipsius modestiam. Quod est in supremis Domini Sol oriens, hoc in ornatu domus sua pulchritudo bona mulieris.

page.notes: Woodcut initial "O" at the start of the concio, framed, shown as a decorative block. The first line of the concio is set with a large initial; it is read here as "OMITAS", the first letters of the first word. The text of the running head is read as "NVPTIALES." in small capitals. Several words are in the original spelling and are left as printed, such as "ornamentum est", "pudenda", "eft" read as est, and "vxor". Doubtful readings: "est quasi" and "eft quafi"; "tanti ponatur est vllum" is read with care because the line is blurred. Line ends are hyphenated only where the print shows a hyphen; none is visible here, so none is written.
